title: Step 63-E Checkout identity contract repair and OTP/session flow
description: HIGH-risk Step 63-E. Repair only the evidence-confirmed OTP OpenAPI/generated-contract drift needed by Checkout Identity, then productionize /checkout/identity using the existing server-only customer-session bridge, backend-authoritative OTP/session, explicit guest-cart merge after successful OTP, and fail-closed recovery. No backend identity business-rule rewrite, database migration, dependency change, address/delivery/review/payment implementation, or client-side credential authority.

dependencies.evidence: PR #307 protected workflow_dispatch 37124556397; merge job 111207127016 SUCCESS; exact-SHA postmerge 111207185618 SUCCESS; terminal Lock release comment 5969434006.

acceptance_criteria.description: OTP request OpenAPI/generated contract matches canonical runtime: successful request returns challenge_id and expires_at with the runtime status; OTP verify response is typed without exposing session_token to browser code.

Checkout Identity uses only server-side createCustomerSessionBridge for OTP/session transport; customer session Set-Cookie is relayed only through the existing sanitizer and no token appears in route data, URL, logs, localStorage, sessionStorage or document.cookie.
A valid OTP establishes authoritative backend session, then guest Cart merge occurs explicitly and only after identity confirmation; unknown merge outcome never fabricates success.

Already-authenticated sessions proceed without OTP; unauthenticated, validation, rate-limit, submitting and recovery states are explicit and accessible; no order/payment exists before identity confirmation.

Address, delivery, review, reservation/order and payment routes remain deferred placeholders and no backend identity business rule, database, dependency, workflow or current-state documentation changes occur.

Any recovered Step56/57 hash drift caused solely by OpenAPI bytes is repaired only with generator-equivalent provenance hash/manifest synchronization on explicitly authorized paths; no design semantics change.

Canonical completion requires exact-head Canonical CI, Phase A, Storefront Quality, CodeQL Security, deterministic Review, exact-artifact Human Gate, ACTIVE Lock, protected merge, exact-SHA postmerge verification and terminal Lock release.

external_gate_evidence.rule: Step 63-E is HIGH risk because it changes the canonical OTP contract and authentication-facing Storefront flow. Final owner HUMAN approval must bind to the frozen exact head/artifact after technical/security gates are green. Direct-main write/raw merge prohibited.

audit_findings.runtime_request_otp: AuthController POST auth/otp/request returns AuthService.requestOtp result {challenge_id, expires_at}; Nest POST default status is 201 because no @HttpCode override is present.
audit_findings.openapi_request_otp: Repaired in Stage E: 201 typed envelope with challenge_id/expires_at plus runtime-aligned 401/429 responses.
audit_findings.runtime_verify_otp: AuthController sets the customer session only via HttpOnly cookie and returns {session_id, expires_at}; invalid/expired OTP is 401 and exhausted attempts are 429.
audit_findings.openapi_verify_otp: Repaired in Stage E: typed 200 envelope with session_id/expires_at, exactly-six-digit code constraint, and runtime-aligned 401/429 responses.
audit_findings.disposition: Scoped OpenAPI/generated/test repair is required before production Checkout Identity can safely consume challenge_id. Backend business logic change is not justified.
